title: Billing Standards for the Contingency Placement Agreements — Invoices, Due Dates, Late-Charge Start and Fee Payments
content:
## 1. Invoicing

1.1 A gross-remittance agreement under the Contingency Placement Agreements is invoiced once per remittance period, within the tier's invoice-issue period, in business days after the period ends, for the period's contingency fees plus the direct-pay fees booked in the period.

1.2 When a calendar month with any collections has produced less than the tier's minimum monthly fee in fees, the month's last invoice is raised to that minimum.

1.3 Direct-pay fees of a net-remittance agreement are retained with the next period's fees.

## 2. Due date

An invoice falls due the tier's fee-invoice due days, in calendar days, after the invoice date.

## 3. Late-charge start

3.1 A late charge accrues on an unpaid invoice only when the handling date is later than the late-charge start counted from the invoice date.

3.2 The late-charge start is the invoice date plus the tier's fee-invoice due days in calendar days plus the tier's late-charge grace days in calendar days. The invoice date is read from the invoice entry in the agreement's client money history, matched on the agreement and the invoice number.

3.3 The comparison is strict: a handling date that falls on the late-charge start itself does not satisfy it; the day after does.

3.4 The former clause under which, from the late-charge start, a charge of the tier's late-charge percent of the unpaid invoice amount, and at least the tier's late-charge minimum, accrues once for each full calendar month the invoice stays unpaid, is **no longer in force**; it is superseded by the current basis on which each monthly late charge on a past-due fee invoice is figured.

## 4. Applying fee payments

Fee payments are applied to the invoice the client names, and otherwise to the oldest unpaid invoice first.

## 5. Offset against remittance — retired

The former clause under which, where the tier allows fees to be offset against remittance, Ridgeline may deduct a past-due invoice from the next gross remittance, booking the deduction as a fee payment whose payment reference is that remittance's statement number, is **no longer in force**; it is superseded by the current basis on which the trust balance of a gross-remittance agreement is set against open invoiced fees.

## 6. Disputed fee lines

A fee line the client disputes within the tier's fee dispute window, in calendar days after the invoice date, is resolved by credit, never by editing the invoice.

## Hypothetical late-charge start cases

An invoice under a tier with 30 due days and 10 grace days has its late-charge start 40 calendar days after the invoice date.

| Handling date | Later than the late-charge start? | Late charge may accrue? |
|---|---|---|
| 39 days after the invoice date | no | no |
| 40 days after the invoice date (the start itself) | no | no |
| 41 days after the invoice date | yes | yes |

## Hypothetical payment application

A client with two unpaid invoices, one older and one newer, pays without naming an invoice: the payment goes to the older invoice first. Had the client named the newer invoice, the payment would be applied to the newer invoice.

Where fees_offset_against_remittance is true, Ridgeline may deduct a past-due invoice from the next gross remittance, booking the deduction as a fee payment whose payment_ref is that remittance's statement number.
